exposure: Mode of interprofessional learning (online vs. in-person)
Student program type (health, social care, teacher education)
outcome: Mean scores concerning learning about child-related topics and skills required for Interprofessional Collaboration (IPC)
Reported progress in Interprofessional Learning (IPL) courses
Experience of gain in IPL learning outcomes
cohort: Nearly 7000 students from health, social care, and teacher education programs participated across their first, second, and third curriculum years.
finding: Online interprofessional learning (IPL) yielded lower mean scores than in-person IPL, and observed decreases in learning outcomes over curriculum years were attributed to students not experiencing a gain in IPL learning rather than the online delivery mode.
cross-section timing: Data was collected annually from 2018 to 2022, across students' first, second, and third curriculum years.
